title: 2b. Direction matters: tool agent
subtitle: The conventional agent answers the same question. There is no plan to inspect and no check between the question and what was computed.
note: Scene 2 of 4 (contrast): a transcript instead of a plan, and nothing that verifies the direction.

evidence.directed: only 0.0% of rows are reciprocated: either undirected stored once (likely) or a directed graph with no mutual edges; column names ['trust'] denote an asymmetric relation
evidence.weighted: numeric column 'trust' with 10 distinct values in [1.0, 10.0]
evidence.weight_semantics: integer counts starting at 1 look like interaction counts (strength), not distances

viz.note: The answer names no nodes; showing the neighbourhood of the highest-degree nodes.

assumptions.measure: out-strength (sum of outgoing trust weights), used because out-degree is tied
assumptions.tie_note: By plain count, nearly everyone is tied: the out-degree maximum is 3, and 597 of 600 nodes (e.g. T10, T100, T101, ...) are in the top histogram bin (2.7 to 3.0), so they trust 3 people each.

result.clarification: Counting the people someone trusts gives a 597-way tie at 3, so it doesn't pick anyone out. The answer T564 instead uses total trust given (out-strength 30). If you meant the plain count, the answer is a 597-way tie at 3 people each.
